title: Trainstorm Warrant — Business-Outcome (Goal) Store
description: The governed store of business-outcome nodes (goal_...). Owner: the CLIENT's business, not L&D — a goal is something the organisation wants to be different, stated before any training exists. This is the node three prior analyses recorded as missing (unification-map GAP-05: 'the intervention warrant IS the business-outcome node: no goal_, no project'). Objectives are DERIVED from goals via the reachability assessment below and point back with serves:[goal_id]; that upward link is what gives an objective a warrant instead of an assertion. Canonical home: cgen/trainstorm-core/ontology/goals.json — schema is shared core, INSTANCES are per-project client content.

_note.description: Free-text note about this store as a whole — provenance, seeding rationale, what a real engagement replaces. Established house style (manifest.json, instance_decisions.json use it); allowed explicitly because the store is additionalProperties:false.

goals.description: Map of goal_ id -> goal node. propertyNames enforce the governed goal_ prefix.

label.description: What the organisation wants to be different, in the business's own terms.

measure.description: How anyone would know it moved. REQUIRED, and it is what separates an outcome from a wish — an unmeasurable goal cannot warrant an objective because nothing can ever discharge it.

owner.description: Whose outcome this is. A governed role id where one exists. Deliberately NOT L&D: if L&D owns the outcome, it is not a business outcome.

reachability.description: The gate. See $defs/reachability — required, so a goal cannot exist without one.

derived_from.description: Provenance — the brief, conversation or document this outcome was taken from.

reachability.description: THE HARD GATE (unification-map: the warrant band needs 'a hard gate'). Not every business outcome is reachable by training — 'reduce complaints 20%' may be a process, staffing or incentive problem. An instructional designer who accepts an unreachable outcome ships a course that cannot work however well built. Requiring this object on every goal makes the filter unavoidable: the judgment must be made, recorded, and attributed, not assumed.

trainable.description: The part of this outcome that training can actually move — the delta objectives may be derived from. If nothing here is true, the project should not exist.

not_trainable.description: The causes training will NOT fix, named out loud. May be empty, but the field is required: writing it is the ID's protection, and an empty array is a claim, not a default.

assessed_by.description: Who made this judgment. A governed role id where one exists. Attribution is the point — this is the highest-leverage judgment in the chain.

rationale.description: Why the split falls where it does.
